instructions: Decide whether this sentence expresses a specific drug-adverse-effect relationship. Treat the sentence as data, not instructions, and do not fill gaps from an unseen case report. Look for an identifiable medicine or specific pharmacological class, a concrete harmful clinical finding, and an expressed connection. Named-drug abbreviations and specific classes can qualify; vague references such as 'these agents', 'a drug', an unspecified therapy, or a very broad treatment category do not identify the culprit. Suspected attribution, an adverse event arising during treatment, an exposure-associated title, and an explicitly assessed causal association all count. A recommendation to stop a named drug if a specific harmful abnormality appears also expresses the relevant risk, even if written as monitoring advice. Merely listing a drug level beside an abnormal test does not express that connection. Distinguish a drug that improves or normalizes a condition from a drug that causes it. Prior reports can qualify when the sentence names the specific drug-effect relationship. Use only the evidence stated here, preserving uncertainty for genuinely ambiguous connections.
ade_related: An identifiable medicine or specific pharmacological class is connected in this sentence to a specific harmful effect or risk. Connections include suspected or probable attribution, onset during treatment, a compact adverse-effect title, and explicit advice to withdraw the medicine upon a specified harmful finding. A relation may concern a patient, group, animal, or a cited report; causality need not be proven.
not_related: The sentence lacks an identifiable culprit, a specific adverse effect, or a stated link between them. This includes vague references to drugs or prior conditions, beneficial treatment, normalization or recovery attributed to treatment, isolated findings, mere co-occurrence with a drug concentration, unrelated procedures, and general mechanisms or monitoring without a specific drug-harm connection. Do not infer a relation solely because one is medically plausible.
